bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to state government; clarifying the legislature's authority to place proposed statutory changes on the ballot for a public vote; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 3B.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[3B.001] LEGISLATIVE REFERRAL.

Subdivision 1.

Definition.

"Measure" means a proposal to amend one or more existing laws, create one or more new laws, or repeal one or more laws, all related to one general subject.

Subd. 2.

Referral.

A majority of the members elected to each house of the legislature may pass a bill or resolution that directs the secretary of state to place the measure on the ballot for the next general election for adoption or rejection by a majority vote of those voting. If a majority of the voters voting on the referred measure approve the measure's adoption, the measure is enacted into law.

Subd. 3.

Publication.

Referred measures adopted by the people must be published by the revisor of statutes in Laws of Minnesota and codified like other laws.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.
additions: "Measure" means a proposal to amend one or more existing laws, create one or more new laws, or repeal one or more laws, all related to one general subject.

A majority of the members elected to each house of the legislature may pass a bill or resolution that directs the secretary of state to place the measure on the ballot for the next general election for adoption or rejection by a majority vote of those voting. If a majority of the voters voting on the referred measure approve the measure's adoption, the measure is enacted into law.
Referred measures adopted by the people must be published by the revisor of statutes in Laws of Minnesota and codified like other laws.
This section is effective the day following final enactment.
